records.description: INSEAD Scholarships are a key source of financial assistance for Master in Management candidates and are awarded either automatically (Diversity and Achievement Scholarships) or through named funds (Kung Family, L'Oréal for Youth, MIM Women's Merit, Qinqin and Xin Zhang). Applications are submitted through the same online portal as the programme application, several funds are limited to earlier admission rounds, and the average award for the MIM'27 class was 13,300 euros, held by 36% of the class against a tuition fee of 57,870 euros for the Class of MIM 2028.

verification.notes: insead.edu returned HTTP 403 on all direct fetches (three attempts across two pages). Figures were therefore taken from content the official insead.edu domain itself publishes in search results, per protocol, and confidence is marked medium. The official MIM FAQ states: '36% of the current MIM'27 Class received a scholarship, averaging 13,300.' The scholarships page confirms the named-fund structure and the Rounds 1-2 / Rounds 1-3 eligibility windows. Earlier cached records quoted an average of about 14,500 euros; the current official FAQ figure of 13,300 euros was used.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the INSEAD Scholarships of Excellence): there is no standalone scholarship deadline - scholarships live and die with the admission round you apply in, so treat your admission round as your scholarship deadline. The numbers frame your expectations: 36% of the MIM'27 class holds a scholarship with an average award of 13,300 euros, against a Class of 2028 tuition fee of 57,870 euros, so even a successful award is partial and you will still fund the rest. Apply early: funds like L'Oréal for Youth only consider candidates admitted in Rounds 1-2, and the MIM Women's Merit Scholarship is limited to Rounds 1-3, so a late round can cost you eligibility even with a strong file. The Diversity and Achievement Scholarships are granted automatically to candidates who bring diversity of background or demonstrate excellence in academics and personal accomplishments, so the main scholarship work is making those qualities visible in the application itself. Use the financial aid office (mim.financialaid@insead.edu per the scholarships page) for loan and payment planning, since scholarships only cover part of the tuition and none of the roughly 22,000 euros of living expenses.

records.description: ENS de Lyon and its partners offer scholarships of excellence for excellent international students to enrol in Master's programmes. The Ampère Scholarships of Excellence pay 1,000 euros per month for one academic year (renewable under conditions), while the SFRI-funded GRADUATE+ scholarships pay 1,000 euros per month for 10 months to students selected for Master's programmes in the Lyon graduate initiatives (CORE, DynLifeSys, MathInfi, PACE). Applications use a single online form covering both the Master's admission and the scholarship.

verification.notes: Verified on both official ENS de Lyon pages on 10 October 2026: Ampère 1,000 euros per month for 12 months (renewable under conditions), GRADUATE+ 1,000 euros per month for 10 months funded under the SFRI programme (ANR-21-SFRI-0001), the 2026-2027 calendar (14 November 2025 - 23 January 2026, results mid-March 2026), the 2027-2028 calendar due in November 2026, the single online application form, the documents list, and the eligible Master's programmes including PACE M2-only and MathInfi M1-M2 tracks.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the ENS de Lyon Scholarships of Excellence): the two strands behave differently even though both pay 1,000 euros per month - the Ampère scholarship runs for a full academic year (12 months, renewable under conditions) while GRADUATE+ pays for 10 months within a Lyon graduate initiative, so budget your rent year on the relevant duration. The application is a single online form that covers both the Master's admission and the scholarship, which is efficient but unforgiving: apply on the form matching your profile (European student, non-European with a foreign degree, or non-European with a French degree), because applications on the wrong form are rejected outright, as are late or incomplete files. Check programme eligibility before you start, since Ampère excludes FEADéP and a handful of specific Master's programmes, and GRADUATE+ is tied to particular graduate initiatives such as PACE (M2 only) and MathInfi (M1 and M2). Every document must be in French or English, so certified translations of diplomas and transcripts are part of your preparation time. Watch for the November reopening of the 2027-2028 calendar - the 2026-2027 round closed at 11:59pm CET on 23 January 2026 with results in mid-March, so a strong file submitted in the first weeks is better than a rushed one on deadline day.
